COMMON API REFERENCE:
Blender 5.2.2 API facts, verified in a separate disposable Blender process:
- A mesh scene object is a bpy.types.Object with type 'MESH'; obj.data is its bpy.types.Mesh datablock.
- Vertex groups belong to obj.vertex_groups. Mesh datablocks (obj.data) have no vertex_groups attribute.
- VertexGroup.weight(index) is a method taking an integer vertex index. Do not use weight[index], weights[index], or pass a MeshVertex object.
- VertexGroup.add(index_sequence, weight, type) writes weights; use a sequence of integer indices and the 'REPLACE' mode for setting a value. Do not assign through .weight or invent a .weights array.
- Iterate obj.data.vertices once; each vertex has an integer .index. MeshVertex.groups holds assignment elements with numeric .group indices and .weight values; it does not support group-name membership lookups. Group-name lookup is available on obj.vertex_groups.
- Preserve source mesh data, UVs, weights, all shape keys, original materials and the existing rig. The host saves your derivative; solve(scene) must not call file-saving operators.
- Python's built-in len(sequence_or_collection) returns its number of elements; for example, len(array) or len(vector).
- MeshVertex.groups is a sparse collection of assignments. An assignment position is not a global vertex-group ID. Never use v.groups[group_index] to locate a group's weight. Match each assignment's .group against the desired VertexGroup.index, or use VertexGroup.weight(v.index) while handling missing membership as zero.
- Vertex IDs and group IDs are different: v.index identifies a vertex; group.index identifies a named vertex group. Each entry a in v.groups is an assignment object with group ID a.group and weight a.weight. To check membership, compare a.group with group.index, for example any(a.group == group.index for a in v.groups). Read a.group and a.weight as attributes; assignment objects are not (group_id, weight) tuples. Do not test integer membership with in on Blender collections or VertexGroup objects.

GENERAL GUIDANCE FOR IDENTIFYING MODEL PARTS:
- Object names, material names, vertex-group names, bones and shape-key names belong to different collections. A label in material_names identifies a material, not a vertex group or separate object. Never assume a name exists in another collection.
- Inspect the mesh object named in the input summary at execution time. obj.data.polygons describes source faces; polygon.material_index selects an entry in obj.material_slots, whose .material identifies that face's material. Check slot bounds and missing materials. A single material may cover several disconnected regions.
- obj.vertex_groups contains named per-object weight groups. Each mesh vertex's sparse groups assignments have numeric .group IDs and .weight values; compare those IDs with VertexGroup.index. A deform group generally describes influence, not an exact semantic body-part boundary. Absence of a guessed group does not identify the requested region.
- Identify a region using measured evidence: actual material assignments, face/vertex adjacency, connected regions, positions, normals and spatial relationships. Inspect actual bounds and object transforms before interpreting coordinates; mesh coordinates are local, and obj.matrix_world maps them to world space. Names can guide investigation but cannot prove which faces cause a visual artifact.
- BMesh vertices and Mesh vertices use different APIs. BMesh deform assignments, when present, live in a deform custom-data layer obtained through bm.verts.layers.deform.active; BMVert has no MeshVertex.groups interface. Do not transfer attribute assumptions between these types.
- Verify a proposed selection is nonempty and matches the intended region before modifying anything. Do not substitute arbitrary thresholds, assumed group membership or guessed counts for geometric investigation. Do not silently claim a repair after an early return that changes nothing.
- All original task restrictions still apply: preserve source vertex/polygon identities, UVs, weights, shape keys, materials and rig. If needed, implement allowed changes through a native evaluated modifier rather than destructive source topology edits. Compute the required return value from actual before/after evaluated geometry. This guidance supplies no task-specific face selection or reference repair algorithm.

GENERAL BMESH ELEMENT AND GEOMETRY CONVENTIONS:
- BMVert, BMEdge and BMFace are different element types. A BMVert has local-space coordinates in .co. A BMEdge has endpoint vertices in .verts. A BMFace has corner vertices in .verts; it has no .co attribute.
- Adjacency collections contain the element type in their name: vert.link_faces yields BMFace objects; vert.link_edges yields BMEdge objects; face.verts yields BMVert objects. Name loop variables for their actual type and check the element type before accessing attributes.
- For a face's individual corner coordinates, iterate its vertices and read each vertex.co. For a representative face center, use a documented BMFace method such as calc_center_median(); a center and a set of corners answer different geometric questions. A face normal is face.normal, and face area is obtained with face.calc_area().
- Keep coordinate spaces consistent. Mesh/BMesh vertex coordinates are local to the object; obj.matrix_world @ vertex.co gives a world-space position. Measure bounds and relationships in a common space before selecting regions. Do not assume a fixed axis cutoff identifies a semantic part on an unfamiliar character.
- Keep BMesh lifetime and source preservation explicit: a BMesh created with bmesh.new() must not be accessed after bm.free(). Calling bm.to_mesh(obj.data) writes to the source mesh; topology-changing operations would violate this task's source-identity restrictions. Inspection does not require writing the BMesh back. A successful API call alone does not establish a repair.
- Recheck every proposed operation against the original task: identify the actual geometric cause using measured evidence, preserve protected source data, use only allowed evaluated changes, and compute the required return value from actual before/after evaluated geometry. Do not replace investigation with placeholders, arbitrary thresholds or guessed counts. No task-specific repair algorithm is supplied by this reference.
